topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy
lecture_lines: Think of a squirrel gathering nuts.
Its velocity is the rate of position change.
We call this rate the derivative.
Accumulated distance is the integral of velocity.
They are two sides of one coin.
animations: Create a dot representing position on a horizontal line #FF5733.
Show a velocity vector moving the dot to the right #33FF57.
Draw a path of the dot's movement to visualize velocity #3357FF.

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse Operation
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.
Differentiation finds the slope at a point.
Integration sums up tiny pieces to reconstruct.
A powerful mathematical harmony emerges here.
animations: Show a function curve f(x) in light blue #ADD8E6.
Create an area under the curve using rectangles #FFFF00.
Demonstrate rectangles getting thinner to approximate the area #FFA500.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
lecture_lines: Integrating a rate gives net change.
Area under the curve measures total accumulation.
This is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Show f(x) and its integral function F(x) #FFFFFF.
Highlight small increment dx on the x-axis #FF00FF.
Show the small area increment dF = f(x)dx #00FFFF.
Connect derivative of F(x) to f(x) #FFFF00.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Derivative equals slope or rate of change.
Integral equals area or total accumulation.
The Fundamental Theorem links these perfectly.
animations: Fade in visual summary of derivative and integral processes #FFFFFF.
Animate the two concepts merging into one #FFFF00.
